graph.title: McLaren Senna (LEGO Speed Champions 75892)

parts.label: steering column (inventory number printed as 73081, digits cut off)

notes: Source is 75892-1 McLaren Senna. The booklet builds two separate models: a small wind-tunnel fan display (pp.5-10, b1-b23) and the car (pp.11-61). The display is a free-standing stand that is never attached to the car, so the graph keeps two disconnected groups on purpose. The driver minifigure (p.4) is built separately and is only placed in the car.
Stickers (numbered 1-20) are not parts and are left out; where a sticker goes on a piece, it is mentioned in that piece's label.
Element IDs come from the inventory page (p.63). Many are not in the catalogue, so they are new part types. Names and ports are my best reading of the pictures.

Most studded parts have one 'stud.1' / 'anti-stud.1' port standing for the whole array of studs. Many parts sit on the same plate, so the receiving (host) side of every stud/anti-stud edge uses a null port. Only the added part's own port is named, and each named port is used once. Where one part joins two others (b39, b40, b99, b103, b141), the second edge has a null port on that part.
The steps are small pictures, so exactly which piece each part presses onto is inferred. Each piece is joined to the piece it visibly sits on or beside.
The 6052126 plates (step 6) are fitted upside-down under the chassis. The 663626 tiles (step 7) are on their side studs, which have no named ports.
The nose (steps 21-31, b77-b98) is built separately. It joins the chassis through the front technic bracket b99, which sits on the orange 2x4 plate b51 (step 32).

Wheels (step 73) are a repeat of 4. Each pin goes into a hole in a technic bracket: copies 1-2 use the rear bracket b49 and copies 3-4 use the front bracket b99. Rim-tyre and cover-rim edges, the rear-section joins to the tan bracket (b181/b182 side holes to b65 side studs), and the minifigure neck/hip joins all use null ports, because the port kinds are not compatible pairs in the rules.
The clip plates 6157554 are given a bar port, so the wing stays 6006739 clip onto them (clip/bar).

Piece-count fix: the 2x small dark plates on the side studs in step 68 (b192, b193) are now the inventory's 2x 306926 (tile 1x2, black), so 4210719 has 12 and 306926 has 2, matching the parts page. That identification is by count, since the pictures are tiny.

The parts page prints '1x 6253240' for the wheel covers, but step 73 clearly builds 4 wheels with 4 covers ('4x'), so the graph keeps 4 covers. The 1x on the page looks like a printing/reading error (the picture shows a cluster of covers).
The inventory prints the steering column as '73081', which is cut off and not a valid element ID. It is modelled as the catalogue type lego-steering-wheel-on-plate (black steering wheel on a plate).
The big canopy b161 (and the small b160) are lift-off pieces, drawn on p.61. They are modelled as joined by studs because they press onto studs.
The driver minifigure sits in the cockpit but is not fastened to the car, so it is a `contact` edge only. The wrench (400626) is held in a hand and is also used on p.61 to remove a wheel cover.

graph_initial.title: McLaren Senna (LEGO Speed Champions 75892)
notes: Source is 75892-1 McLaren Senna. The booklet has two models: a small wind-tunnel fan display (pp.5-10, b1-b23) and the car (pp.11-61). The display is not connected to the car. All edges are modelled.
Stickers (numbered 1-20) are not parts and are left out; where a sticker goes on a piece, it is mentioned in that piece's label.
Element IDs come from the inventory page (p.63). Many are not in the catalogue, so they are new part types. Names and ports are my best reading of the pictures.

The steps are small pictures, so exactly which stud of which piece each part presses onto is inferred. Each piece is joined to the piece it visibly sits on or beside. Port names are mostly generic (stud.1 / anti-stud.1).
Parts that sit on the same lower piece are drawn as separate edges to its stud.1 even though they use different physical studs.
The 6052126 plates (step 6) are fitted upside-down under the chassis. The 663626 tiles (step 7) are clipped to their side studs, which have no named ports, so those edges use null ports.
The nose (steps 21-31, b77-b98) is built separately. It joins the chassis through the front technic bracket b99, which sits on the orange 2x4 plate b51 (step 32).

Wheels (step 73) are a repeat of 4. Each pin goes into a hole in a technic bracket. Copies 1-2 use the rear bracket b49 and copies 3-4 use the front bracket b99. The wheel-cover edge has no named port on the rim.
The inventory lists 12x 4210719 (plate 1x1), but the steps seem to use 14: steps 4, 8, 37, 38, 43, 50 and 68. I have used it for step 68 as well, so b192 and b193 add two to the 12 listed.

The inventory lists 2x 306926 (tile 1x2, black) but I could not place it in any step, so it is not in the graph. The inventory lists 1x 6253240, but 4 wheel covers are used in step 73 and shown with the parts.

The inventory shows 6147050, 6194, 6030985 and 6171717 only in small print. Step 8 (display) has the only confident use of 6147050, as the two curved pieces over the fan stand. The step 27/28 slopes and round plates are assigned by shape.
The big canopy b161 (and the small b160) are lift-off pieces, drawn on p.61. They are modelled as joined by studs because they press onto studs.
The driver minifigure (p.4) sits in the cockpit but is not fastened to the car, so it is a `contact` edge only. The wrench (400626) is held in a hand and is also used on p.61 to remove a wheel cover.
